verdict.headline: Doubts about AI spending return as Lam, Tesla and Meta pull tech futures sharply lower
verdict.label: Pre-market: Nasdaq 100 futures about -1.7% to -1.9%, S&P 500 futures about -1.0%, Dow futures -356 points; Lam ~-9%, Tesla ~-3% to -5%, Meta ~-2%; Kospi -3.52%, Nikkei -2.65%; Brent ~$112.27 (+3.2%); 10Y ~5.05-5.07% (-8 to -9 bp); BTC $81,817.
verdict.rationale_short:
What happened: Nasdaq 100 futures fell 1.7% to 1.9% and S&P 500 futures about 1%, enough to erase Wednesday's 1.05% Nasdaq gain. Lam Research fell about 9% premarket after a December-quarter guide that only matched estimates, Tesla fell 3% to 5% after cutting its 2026 spending floor to $20 billion from $25 billion, and Meta slipped about 2% after creating a non-voting share class it can use to fund its AI buildout. The Kospi fell 3.52% and the Nikkei 2.65% as Samsung and SK hynix dropped 4% to 5.5%. Brent rose 3.2% to $112.27 on unconfirmed Iranian claims that seven tankers were hit, yet the 10-year fell about 9 basis points.

What it means: Wednesday's gain paid for AI revenue already reported; overnight the question moved to how the building is funded, and the market marked down both a spending cut and a new funding tool. Super Micro's 27% revenue raise still stands, so the evidence cuts both ways. Treasuries are acting as a refuge from stocks, so oil is not setting yields today.

What would change the picture: a Nasdaq close below Tuesday's 26,424.82 and an S&P 500 close below 7,666.45 would show Wednesday's rebound failed. Holding both would show reported revenue still outweighs the funding worry. A 10-year break below 5.0% would show stock fears outweighing oil.
verdict.lede_short: Tech futures fell nearly 2% as Lam Research's in-line guide, Tesla's $5 billion spending cut and Meta's new funding share class put the cost of AI building back at the center, and Seoul's chipmakers erased Wednesday's rally overnight. Oil rose 3% on unconfirmed tanker attacks, yet Treasury yields fell, a sign buyers are seeking safety. A Nasdaq close below 26,424.82 would mean Wednesday's rebound failed.

supporting_data.label: Reuters had Nasdaq futures down more than 1%, with Tesla off 5.3%, Meta 1.9%, Intel 5.1%, and AMD, Qualcomm, Marvell, Broadcom and Micron between 2.9% and 5.3% — the selling is spread across chip makers, not confined to the three companies that reported.

Tesla now expects 2026 capital spending in excess of $20 billion, down from in excess of $25 billion in its second-quarter filing — a $5 billion cut by one of the largest AI and robotics spenders was read as a slower pace, not as discipline.

Meta's board approved a listed, non-voting Class C stock effective January 19, 2027 — with free cash flow negative last quarter, the market took a new funding tool as a sign that spending will outrun cash.
The Kospi fell 3.52% to 5,533.77 and the Nikkei 2.65% to 62,907.84, with SK hynix down 5.49% and Samsung 4.03% — Seoul closed below Tuesday's level, erasing Wednesday's 3.29% recovery in one session.

Lam Research guided the December quarter to $8.6 billion, plus or minus $400 million, after record revenue of $8.22 billion — an in-line guide was not enough for chip equipment, the part of the trade priced furthest ahead, and the stock fell about 9% premarket.

Brent rose 3.2% to $112.27 after Iran's Revolutionary Guard said seven tankers were hit overnight, a claim no shipper or government had confirmed — yet the 10-year yield fell about 9 basis points, so bond buyers are seeking safety rather than pricing oil-driven inflation.

trade_setups.invalidation: Closes below both would show Wednesday's rebound failed; holding both would show reported revenue still outweighs the funding worry.
